user.text: When navigating from the dashboard to a project, I want the project's title to appear instantly, but I don't want to prefetch the rest of the project page.

history.assistant:
The project title now loads with the prefetch, so it shows instantly when you click through from the dashboard. The description and activity list aren't prefetched; they load after you click.

Changes:

- app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx
  - I added export const prefetch = 'partial'. This lets a link to this route prefetch only part of the page and fill in the slug.
  - I split the page into two components, each in its own <Suspense> block. ProjectTitle reads the slug and calls getProjectTitle, so it's included in the prefetch.
  - ProjectDetails calls await navigation() (from next/cache) before loading anything. So the slow getProjectDetails call only runs after you click. Until then the prefetched page shows "Loading details...".
- app/page.tsx: the dashboard links now use prefetch={true}. With a plain link, only the part of the page that doesn't depend on the slug would be prefetched, so the title would still show "Loading project..." at first.

I used the Next docs bundled with your installed version (16.4.0-canary.52); navigation() and the prefetch route setting both arrived in 16.4.

npx next build succeeded (exit 0) and shows /projects/[slug] as a partial prerender (◐). I haven't checked in a browser that the title appears instantly and the details load only after the click. Next only prefetches in production, so you'd need next build && next start to see it.

The build also reformatted tsconfig.json on its own: it set "jsx": "react-jsx" (which Next requires), added .next/dev/types//.ts, and created next-env.d.ts and .next/. Your earlier edit to package.json and the untracked package-lock.json are unchanged.

On pages where all the content is statically renderable, Next.js serves prefetches from the static cache. If a page accesses non-static data, it's prefetched at runtime. exit_code=0 --- title: prefetch description: API Reference for the prefetch function, which keeps a subtree out of a route's App Shell so it renders on a per-link prefetch or a navigation. related: links: - app/api-reference/functions/navigation - app/api-reference/functions/connection - app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching - app/api-reference/functions/io - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents --- Calling `await prefetch()` defers the code below it to a per-link prefetch or a navigation, instead of rendering it in the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The fallback of the nearest [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary takes its place in the shell, and the deferred content renders once one of those happens. It is meant to defer content that the App Shell would otherwise render, typically content that depends on session data and is expensive to generate.
